sentences.text: The vs Delhi on 19 July, 2023

The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.671 of 2012
Judgment:

The appellants are the claimants in M.V.O.P.No.447 of 2007 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Judge, Family Court-cum-IV Additional District & Sessions Judge,
Vijayawada and the respondents are respondents in the said case.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- Judge, Family Court-cum-IV Additional District & Sessions Judge,
Vijayawada
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The aforesaid M.V.O.P.No.447 of 2007 was filed by the claim petitioners, under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.7,00,000/- for the death of Kodi Jhansi, who died in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 16.03.2007.
1st claim petitioner is the husband and 2nd claim petitioner is the minor son of the deceased.

4. The brief averments of the claim petition are as follows:
On 16.03.2007 at about 1:30 a.m., while the deceased and her mother-in-law were going to Hyderabad from Vijayawada in RTC Bus bearing No.AP 11 Z 4943, on the way the driver of Bus drove it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed behind a stationed Lorry bearing No.AP 24 U 7797 belongs to 2nd respondent and as a result of which Jhansi died on the spot, and others sustained grievous injuries.
A case in Crime No.51/2007 was registered by Chivemla Police.

1st respondent is the APSRTC,
2nd respondent is the owner of the Lorry and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the Lorry.
5. 1st respondent filed a counter by denying the claim of claimants and pleaded that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the APSRTC, negligence was on the part of the lorry only.
6. 2nd respondent filed a counter by denying that there was no negligence on the part of the 2nd respondent and pleaded that the claim is highly excessive.

7. 3rd respondent filed a counter by denying that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the APSRTC bus only and there was no rash and negligence on the part of the stationed Lorry and pleaded that the driver of 2nd respondent had no valid and effective driving license.

8. Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the Tribunal framed the following issues for trial:

1

1. Whether the death of Kodi Jhansi in a motor vehicle accident on 16.03.2007 at 1:30 hours on NH-9 road at Gunjulur Sivaru, Nalgonda District due to the rash and negligent driving of crime vehicle i.e., RTC Bus?
2. If so, what is the correct age and income of the deceased by the date of accident?
3. If so, whether the petitioners are entitled to the compensation as prayed for?

If so,
from whom?

4. To what relief?
9.
During the course of enquiry, on behalf of the claimants, P.W.1 was examined and got marked Exs.A1 to A6.
On behalf of respondents, R.W.1 was examined and Ex.B1 was marked.

10. At the culmination of enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the accident is occurred only due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle APSRTC Bus bearing No.AP 11 Z 4943 and awarded an amount of Rs.3,55,000/- to the claim petitioners towards total compensation for the death of Kodi Jhansi in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 16.03.2007.
Aggrieved by the said decree and order passed by the Tribunal, the claim petitioners filed the present appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
11. Heard both sides.

12. Now, the points for determination are:
1) Whether the order passed by the Tribunal needs any interference?
If so, to what extent?
2) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled enhanced compensation as prayed for?

POINTS:
13.

The evidence of P.W.1 coupled with Ex.A1 Certified Copy of the First Information Report, Ex.A2 Certified Copy of the Post Mortem Report and the Ex.A6 Certified Copy of the Charge Sheet proves that the accident in question is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the APSRTC Bus bearing No. AP 11 Z 4943 and the deceased Kodi Jhansi died in the said road accident.
The Tribunal also came to the same conclusion.
Therefore, I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.
14. Coming to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.3,55,000/- towards total compensation to the claimants against 1st respondent/APSRTC.
The material on record reveals that the deceased was aged about 24 years at the time of accident.

On appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the deceased was The vs Delhi on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122901697/
2 used to earn Rs.2,500/- per month i.e., Rs.30,000/- (Rs.2,500/- x 12) per annum.
The accident was occurred in the year 2007.
Therefore, in those days an ordinary coolie can easily earn Rs.100/- per day.

On considering the entire material available on record and facts and circumstances of the case,
I find it is desirable to enhance the monthly income of the deceased from Rs.2,500/- to Rs.3,000/-.

Therefore, the annual income of the deceased was arrived at Rs.36,000/- (Rs.3,000/- x 12)
notionally.
The dependents on the deceased are two in number.
As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Smt.Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1, 1/3rd income has to the deducted towards loss of dependency.

entities.text: Smt.Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, 1/3rd of Rs.36,000/- = Rs.12,000/- has to be deducted from out of Rs.36,000/-.
Net income available to the dependents on the deceased arrived at Rs.24,000/- (Rs.36,000/- - Rs.12,000/-).
The deceased was aged about 24 years.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of the deceased is '18'.

After applying multiplier of '18', an amount of Rs.4,32,000/- (Rs.24,000/- x 18) is awarded to the claimants towards loss of dependency, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards loss of estate, an amount of Rs.10,000/-
is awarded towards funeral expenses.
For the foregoing reasons, the appellants/claimants are entitled total compensation of Rs.4,62,000/-.

In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation granted by the Tribunal for an amount of Rs.3,55,000/- to Rs.4,62,000/-, consequently the claimants are entitled enhanced compensation of Rs.1,07,000/- along with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

1st respondent/APSRTC is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,07,000/- with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum within two (2) months before the Tribunal from the date of this Judgment.
On such deposit, 2nd appellant is entitled to withdraw the same after attaining majority, till that date the said amount shall be kept in Fixed Deposit.
There shall be no order as to costs.

As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
